patch.value: Beyond-PM exemplar: a content-addressed version-control domain built on pm primitives alone, as executable proof of the universal claim

The universal-platform claim names version control as its headline example: if pm's primitives are truly general, a git-like system is expressible in them. Nothing tests that, and version control is the right test precisely because it stresses the primitives pm cares most about — content-addressed immutable objects, an append-only history with verifiable chaining, a branch as a movable reference into that history, a merge with declared conflict semantics, and point-in-time reconstruction of any state. Every one of those maps onto a capability pm already claims for its own data. Build the exemplar as a package: objects as items with content-addressed identifiers, trees as typed edges, commits as history entries chained by the existing hash construction, branches as references, merge as a declared resolution over the same merge semantics pm uses for its own workspaces, and checkout as point-in-time reconstruction. Success is not a competitive VCS; success is a demonstration that survives a property test — commit a tree, branch, diverge, merge, and reconstruct any prior state exactly — using only public SDK surface. Where it cannot be done without private access, that is the finding, and each gap is filed as SDK promotion work.

The exemplar is a package that imports public SDK surface only, asserted by the existing import-boundary gate with no waiver; Content-addressed objects, trees, commits, branches, merge, and point-in-time checkout are all expressed in pm primitives, with the mapping documented primitive by primitive; A property test commits a tree, branches, diverges, merges, and reconstructs an arbitrary prior state exactly, and runs in CI; Every capability that could not be expressed through public SDK surface is filed as an SDK gap item linked discovered_from this exemplar, and the exemplar documents the workaround it used meanwhile; The exemplar states plainly what it is not — it is a proof of expressiveness, not a production VCS — so the claim it supports stays accurate; A measured statement of scale limits is recorded, so the proof is not mistaken for a performance claim
Prove the universal-domain claim on the hardest domain pm has ever cited, using public SDK surface only
This is the strongest possible evidence for the platform positioning, and equally valuable if it fails, because a falsified claim found now is a corrected roadmap rather than a broken promise
Will surface genuine SDK gaps in content addressing, reference management, and merge semantics; those gaps are the deliverable as much as the exemplar is
The claim that a VCS is buildable on pm primitives is backed by a running package and a property test rather than by an assertion in a milestone
The claim is already published in the milestone and the marketing narrative; proving or falsifying it before v1.0 freezes the SDK surface is far cheaper than after

message: File the VCS exemplar that turns the universal-domain claim into a testable proposition
